description: Blacklight facility layout guide for the O-shaped headquarters, Black-level north shell, inner courtyard access ring, subfloor classification, service infrastructure, and Green support implementation boundaries.

entries.title: Facility Layout Guide: Access Shells, Rings, and Subfloors
entries.summary: The O-shaped headquarters uses public rings, controlled support layers, Black-level access regions, and subfloor boundaries to keep ordinary corporate operations, Green support work, and Black-level operational truth physically separated.
entries.clearance: BLUE CARD public-safe orientation / GREEN CARD support layout detail / BLACK CARD full access-map authority.

body: The Blacklight headquarters is organized as an O-shaped corporate facility with public-facing operations around the outside, controlled internal support layers, an inner courtyard access ring, and a deliberately uneven security profile. From a visitor's perspective, the building reads as a serious secure-technology headquarters. From a Green support perspective, the building is a layered maintenance problem with unusual routing rules. From a Black perspective, the building is a shell around the records, people, rooms, and infrastructure that cannot be safely explained as ordinary secure contract work.

The most important layout note is scope: the entire north shell of the facility and the inner courtyard access ring are Black-level access areas. These are not merely executive-prestige zones or normal secure-client suites. They are Black-level routing, custody, coordination, and interpretive spaces where ordinary corporate explanations are no longer sufficient. Personnel without Black access should only enter those regions under escort, explicit incident authority, or narrowly scoped Green support orders.

Subfloor access follows a similar rule. Subfloor minus one is standard records keeping, server architecture, plumbing, controlled mechanical routing, ordinary utility support, and building service infrastructure. It is still secure and not public, but it is not automatically Black-level. All subfloors below minus one are Black-level unless a specific section is explicitly downgraded for Green support under controlled task authority.

This guide is the bridge between facility-mode records and practical infrastructure implementation. It gives the archive a general layout vocabulary before more specialized records discuss evacuation routing, emergency support, environmental isolation, reserve power, utility decks, courtyard access, and Black-area maintenance boundaries.

entries.summary: The north shell and inner courtyard access ring are Black-level regions that physically concentrate restricted routing, high-level custody, and access-control truth inside the otherwise corporate-readable headquarters.

body: The north shell is the part of the headquarters where the public building stops being a complete explanation. Its doors, elevators, meeting rooms, service corridors, and support spaces may still look like corporate architecture, but the access logic underneath them belongs to Black-level custody and interpretation. A person may cross from ordinary headquarters language into Black-level physical truth without the carpet, walls, or lights announcing the change.

The inner courtyard access ring serves a related purpose. Publicly, the courtyard reads as architectural prestige, staff wellness, daylighting, and controlled circulation around the center of the building. Black-level records treat the inner courtyard access ring as protected internal movement: a route structure that can connect restricted offices, sealed support zones, Black Archive access, courtyard-facing observation, and north-shell movement without exposing those connections to the public outer ring.

Green personnel are often told that the north shell and courtyard ring exist for highest-security clients, executive continuity, secure records, or maintenance-sensitive demonstration infrastructure. Those explanations may be true at the Blue or Green layer, but they are incomplete. Green support orders for these regions should be narrow, timed, logged, and attached to explicit stop conditions.

body: Subfloor minus one is the lowest layer of the building that can still be explained primarily through ordinary secure-facility infrastructure. It contains standard records keeping, server architecture, plumbing, water routing, mechanical support, controlled storage, maintenance access, and utility service functions that a serious secure-technology headquarters could plausibly maintain without requiring Black-level truth.

That does not make subfloor minus one public. It is controlled space. White-card employees generally have no reason to enter it. Blue personnel may have task-based access for records, IT, compliance, or secure support. Green personnel may maintain utility, server, mechanical, and environmental systems. Black personnel may use it as the last clean explanatory layer before deeper access becomes impossible to justify as ordinary infrastructure.

All subfloors below minus one are Black-level by default. Subfloor minus two and below may include deep reserve infrastructure, Black Archive support, sealed mechanical routes, emergency continuity rooms, protected stores, hidden access controls, specialized environmental systems, incident custody spaces, or operational infrastructure that cannot be safely described as plumbing, server architecture, or records keeping.

entries.title: General Facilities Layout and Infrastructure Implementation
entries.summary: Facilities implementation uses ordinary building systems as the visible layer around Black-level routing, Green support work, emergency modes, and long-term continuity infrastructure.
entries.clearance: GREEN CARD implementation detail / BLACK CARD full facility-truth integration.

body: Blacklight infrastructure implementation is built on dual readability. Every system should have an ordinary facilities meaning and, where required, a restricted operational meaning. A door is a door, but it is also access control. A ceiling baffle is architecture, but it can become section isolation. A utility deck is service access, but it can become a diagnostic route around a contaminated floor. A server room is records and compute, but it may also be the line between a product instance, a facility interface, and something wearing a familiar voice.

The north shell, inner courtyard access ring, and subfloors below minus one create the Black-level skeleton of the facility. Subfloor minus one creates the standard support membrane: records, servers, plumbing, mechanical service, and utility architecture that Green personnel can maintain under controlled conditions. The outer ring and middle layers preserve the public corporate workplace. The whole building therefore works as nested explanations rather than a single secret room behind a bookshelf.

Implementation records should always state the visible function, the support function, the clearance boundary, the emergency behavior, and the stop condition. Green personnel need to know what to maintain, where to stop, and who to call. Black personnel need to know what a system really supports, how it may fail under abnormal conditions, and what lower-clearance explanation is still honest enough to use.

tables.title: Infrastructure Implementation Principles
rows: Every restricted system should have an ordinary facilities explanation where possible without falsifying maintenance requirements.
Green support orders must include system, location, route, safety boundary, reporting channel, and stop condition.
Black-level systems must preserve custody, source credibility, access history, and incident interpretation.
Doors, elevators, air, power, lighting, communications, and signage must support facility modes without confusing staff into unsafe action.
Subfloor -1 may support ordinary secure infrastructure; subfloor -2 and below default to Black-level unless explicitly downgraded.
Inner courtyard routes must protect Black-level movement without turning the public courtyard into an unexplained forbidden symbol.
